mishnayos.summary: This mishnah asks when we may start saying Shema at night, and until when. The Rabbis also teach that they set an early deadline to keep people from missing the mitzvah.

chunks.en: From what time do we say Shema at night?
chunks.st: From when, that is, from what time, does one recite Shema in the evening?

chunks.en: From the time the Kohanim go in to eat their terumah,
chunks.st: From the time when the priests enter to partake of their teruma.

words.note: Kohanim are the family of Aharon who served in the Beis HaMikdash.
Terumah is a special gift of food given to Kohanim; they may eat it only when they are pure, after nightfall.

chunks.en: until the end of the first watch of the night.
chunks.st: Until when does the time for the recitation of the evening Shema extend? Until the end of the first watch.
chunks.stMore: The term used in the Torah (Deuteronomy 6:7) to indicate the time for the recitation of the evening Shema is beshokhbekha, when you lie down, which refers to the time in which individuals go to sleep. Therefore, the time for the recitation of Shema is the first portion of the night, when individuals typically prepare for sleep.

words.note: The night was split into three watches, like shifts of guards.

chunks.en: That is what Rabbi Eliezer says.
chunks.st: That is the statement of Rabbi Eliezer.

words.note: A great Rabbi of the Mishnah.

chunks.en: But the Sages say,
chunks.st: The Rabbis say:

chunks.en: until midnight.
chunks.st: The time for the recitation of the evening Shema is until midnight.

chunks.en: Rabban Gamliel says,
chunks.st: Rabban Gamliel says:

words.note: A title for the leader of the Jewish people.
A great Rabbi of the Mishnah, head of the Sanhedrin.

chunks.en: until dawn.
chunks.st: One may recite Shema until dawn,
chunks.stMore: indicating that beshokhbekha is to be understood as a reference to the entire time people sleep in their beds, the whole night. The mishna relates that Rabban Gamliel practiced in accordance with his ruling.

words.note: The first light that shows in the sky before sunrise.

chunks.en: Once his sons came home late from a wedding party.
chunks.st: There was an incident where Rabban Gamliel’s sons returned very late from a wedding hall.

chunks.en: They said to him,
chunks.st: They said to him,
chunks.stMore: as they had been preoccupied with celebrating with the groom and bride:

chunks.en: "We did not say Shema yet."
chunks.st: We did not recite Shema.

chunks.en: He said to them,
chunks.st: He said to them:

chunks.en: "If dawn has not come up yet,
chunks.st: If the dawn has not yet arrived,

chunks.en: you still must say it.
chunks.st: you are obligated to recite Shema.
chunks.stMore: Since Rabban Gamliel’s opinion disagreed with that of the Rabbis, he explained to his sons that the Rabbis actually agree with him,

chunks.en: And not only this,
chunks.st: and that it is not only with regard to the halakha of the recitation of Shema,

chunks.en: but everything that the Sages said
chunks.st: but rather, wherever the Sages say

chunks.en: should be done by midnight,
chunks.st: until midnight,

chunks.en: may really be done until dawn.
chunks.st: the mitzva may be performed until dawn.

chunks.en: Burning the fats and limbs of korbanos on the mizbeach
chunks.st: Rabban Gamliel cites several cases in support of his claim, such as the burning of fats and limbs on the altar.

words.note: Special fat parts of a korban that were burned on the mizbeach.
Parts of a korban burned whole on the mizbeach.

chunks.en: may be done until dawn.
chunks.st: Due to the quantity of offerings each day, the priests were often unable to complete the burning of all of the fats and limbs, so they continued to be burned into the night,
chunks.stMore: as it is written: “This is the law of the burnt offering: The burnt offering shall remain upon the pyre on the altar all night until morning, while the fire on the altar burns it” (Leviticus 6:2).

chunks.en: And all korbanos that are eaten for one day and night
chunks.st: And, with regard to all sacrifices, such as the sin-offerings and the guilt-offerings that are eaten for one day and night;

chunks.en: may be eaten until dawn.
chunks.st: although the Sages state that they may be eaten only until midnight, by Torah law they may be eaten until dawn.
chunks.stMore: This is in accordance with the verse: “On the day on which it is offered must you eat. Do not leave it until the morning” (Leviticus 7:15).

chunks.en: If so,
chunks.st: If so,

chunks.en: why did the Sages say "until midnight"?
chunks.st: why did the Sages say that they may be eaten only until midnight?

chunks.he: כְּדֵי לְהַרְחִיק אֶת הָאָדָם מִן הָעֲבֵרָה:
chunks.en: To keep a person far away from sinning.
chunks.st: This is in order to distance a person from transgression,
chunks.stMore: as if one believes that he has until dawn to perform the mitzva, he might be negligent and postpone it until the opportunity to perform the mitzva has passed.

mishnayos.stIntro: The beginning of tractate Berakhot, the first tractate in the first of the six orders of Mishna, opens with a discussion of the recitation of Shema, as the recitation of Shema encompasses an acceptance of the yoke of Heaven and of the mitzvot, and as such, forms the basis for all subsequent teachings. The Mishna opens with the laws regarding the appropriate time to recite Shema:

mishnayos.summary: This mishnah teaches when we may start saying Shema in the morning, and until when.

chunks.en: From what time do we say Shema in the morning?
chunks.st: From when does one recite Shema in the morning?

chunks.en: From when one can tell techeiles blue from white.
chunks.st: From when a person can distinguish between sky-blue [tekhelet] and white.

words.note: Techeiles is the special blue color used in tzitzis.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer says:

words.note: A great Rabbi of the Mishnah.

chunks.en: From when one can tell techeiles blue from leek-green.
chunks.st: From when one can distinguish between sky-blue and leek-green.

words.note: A leek is a green vegetable whose color is close to blue.

chunks.en: And one must finish it by sunrise.
chunks.st: And one must finish reciting Shema until the end of the period when you rise, i.e., sunrise, when the sun begins to shine.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehoshua says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehoshua says:

words.note: A great Rabbi of the Mishnah.

chunks.en: until three hours into the day,
chunks.st: One may recite the morning Shema until three hours of the day, which this is still considered when you rise,

chunks.en: because that is the way of kings and princes:
chunks.st: as that is the habit of kings to rise from their sleep
chunks.basisNote: Steinsaltz says kings; Bartenura says the sons of kings.

chunks.en: to get up three hours into the day.
chunks.st: at three hours of the day.

chunks.en: Someone who says it later did not lose anything;
chunks.st: While there is a set time frame for the recitation of Shema, one who recites Shema from that time onward loses nothing.
chunks.stMore: Although he does not fulfill the mitzva of reciting of Shema at its appointed time,
chunks.basisNote: Bartenura adds: he still says the brachos of Shema.

chunks.en: he is like a person reading from the Torah, and he gets reward for that.
chunks.st: he is nevertheless considered like one who reads the Torah, and is rewarded accordingly.

mishnayos.summary: Beis Shammai and Beis Hillel argue about whether we must lie down at night and stand in the morning to say Shema. The halacha follows Beis Hillel: say it however you are.

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say,
chunks.st: Beit Shammai say:
chunks.stMore: One should recite Shema in the manner indicated in the text of Shema itself. Therefore,

words.note: Beis Shammai were the students of Shammai, a great early Sage.

chunks.en: at night everyone must lie down on his side and say Shema,
chunks.st: in the evening every person must recline on his side and recite Shema,
chunks.stMore: in fulfillment of the verse: “When you lie down,”

chunks.en: and in the morning he must stand,
chunks.st: and in the morning he must stand and recite Shema,
chunks.stMore: in fulfillment of the verse: When you rise,

chunks.en: as it says, "when you lie down and when you get up."
chunks.st: as it is stated: “When you lie down, and when you rise.”

chunks.en: And Beis Hillel say,
chunks.st: And Beit Hillel say:

words.note: Beis Hillel were the students of Hillel, a great early Sage.

chunks.en: everyone says it in whatever way he is,
chunks.explain: Standing, sitting, lying down, or walking.
chunks.st: Every person recites Shema as he is,
chunks.stMore: and he may do so in whatever position is most comfortable for him, both day and night,

chunks.en: as it says, "and when you walk on the road."
chunks.st: as it is stated: “And when you walk along the way,” when one is neither standing nor reclining (Me’iri).

chunks.en: If so,
chunks.st: If so, according to Beit Hillel,

chunks.en: why does it say "when you lie down and when you get up"?
chunks.st: why was it stated: “When you lie down, and when you rise”?

chunks.en: It means at the time people go to sleep,
chunks.st: This is merely to denote time; at the time when people lie down

chunks.en: and at the time people get up.
chunks.st: and the time when people rise.

chunks.en: Rabbi Tarfon said,
chunks.st: With regard to this halakha, Rabbi Tarfon said:

words.note: A great Rabbi of the Mishnah.

chunks.en: "I was traveling on the road,
chunks.st: Once, I was coming on the road

chunks.en: and I lay down on my side to say Shema,
chunks.st: when I stopped and reclined to recite Shema

words.en: and I lay on my side

chunks.en: like Beis Shammai say,
chunks.st: in accordance with the statement of Beit Shammai.
chunks.stMore: Although Rabbi Tarfon was a disciple of Beit Hillel, he thought that fulfilling the mitzva in accordance with the opinion of Beit Shammai would be a more meticulous fulfillment of the mitzva, acceptable to all opinions.

chunks.en: and I put myself in danger from robbers."
chunks.st: Yet in so doing, I endangered myself due to the highwaymen [listim] who accost travelers.

chunks.en: They said to him,
chunks.st: The Sages said to him:

chunks.en: "You deserved to pay with your life,
chunks.st: You deserved to be in a position where you were liable to pay with your life,

chunks.en: because you went against Beis Hillel."
chunks.st: as you transgressed the statement of Beit Hillel.
chunks.stMore: This statement will be explained in the Gemara.

mishnayos.stIntro: Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel disputed the proper way to recite Shema.

mishnayos.summary: This mishnah tells how many brachos we say before and after Shema, and that we must not change the way the Sages wrote each bracha.

chunks.he: בַּשַּׁחַר מְבָרֵךְ שְׁתַּיִם לְפָנֶיהָ וְאַחַת לְאַחֲרֶיהָ,
chunks.en: In the morning one says two brachos before it and one after it,
chunks.st: In the morning when reciting Shema, one recites two blessings beforehand, the first on the radiant lights and the second the blessing on the love of Torah, and one thereafter, which begins with: True and Firm [emet veyatziv].

chunks.en: and at night two before it and two after it.
chunks.st: And in the evening one recites two blessings beforehand, on the radiant lights and on the love of God, and two thereafter, the blessing of redemption: True and Faithful [emet ve’emuna], and the blessing: Help us lie down.

chunks.en: Whether it is said the long way or the short way,
chunks.st: With regard to the blessing: True and Faithful, whether one recites it in its long formula and whether one recites it in its short formula, he fulfills his obligation (Tosafot).

chunks.en: Where the Sages said to make it long,
chunks.st: However, the general principle is: Where the Sages said to recite a long blessing,

chunks.en: one may not make it short.
chunks.st: one may not shorten it,

chunks.en: Where they said to make it short, one may not make it long.
chunks.st: and so too, wherever they said to recite a short blessing, one may not lengthen it.

chunks.en: Where they said to end with "Baruch," one may not skip it.
chunks.st: Where the Sages said that a blessing must conclude with a second blessing at the end, he may not fail to conclude with that blessing.

words.note: Closing a bracha means ending it with "Baruch Atah Hashem..."

chunks.en: And where they said not to end that way,
chunks.st: Similarly, if the Sages said that a blessing must not conclude with a second blessing,

chunks.en: one may not add an ending.
chunks.st: one may not conclude with a blessing.

mishnayos.stIntro: From the laws of the recitation of Shema itself, the mishna proceeds to discuss the blessings recited in conjunction with Shema. Here, the order is established:

mishnayos.summary: We remember leaving Egypt every night too, in the last part of Shema. Ben Zoma learned this from a pasuk, and the Sages learned that we will remember it even in the days of Mashiach.

chunks.en: We mention leaving Egypt at night.
chunks.st: The exodus from Egypt is mentioned at night, adjacent to the recitation of Shema.

chunks.en: Rabbi Elazar ben Azaryah said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya said:

words.note: A great Rabbi of the Mishnah who became head of the Sanhedrin when he was very young.

chunks.en: "I am about seventy years old,
chunks.st: I am approximately seventy years old, and

chunks.he: וְלֹא זָכִיתִי שֶׁתֵּאָמֵר יְצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם בַּלֵּילוֹת,
chunks.en: and I could not prove that leaving Egypt must be said at night,
chunks.st: although I have long held this opinion, I was never privileged to prevail (Me’iri) and prove that there is a biblical obligation to fulfill the accepted custom (Ra’avad) and have the exodus from Egypt mentioned at night,

chunks.en: until Ben Zoma explained it,
chunks.st: until Ben Zoma interpreted it homiletically and proved it obligatory.

words.note: A great Rabbi of the Mishnah, famous for explaining pesukim.

chunks.en: as it says, "So that you will remember
chunks.st: Ben Zoma derived it as it is stated: “That you may remember

chunks.en: the day you left the land of Egypt
chunks.st: the day you went out of the land of Egypt

chunks.en: all the days of your life."
chunks.st: all the days of your life” (Deuteronomy 16:3).

chunks.en: "The days of your life" means
chunks.st: The days of your life,

chunks.en: the days. "All the days of your life"
chunks.st: refers to daytime alone; however, the addition of the word all, as it is stated: All the days of your life,

chunks.en: adds the nights. But the Sages say,
chunks.st: comes to add nights as well. And the Rabbis,
chunks.stMore: who posit that there is no biblical obligation to mention the exodus from Egypt at night, explain the word, all, differently and say:

chunks.en: "The days of your life" means
chunks.st: The days of your life, refers to the days in

chunks.en: this world.
chunks.st: this world,

chunks.en: "All the days of your life"
chunks.st: all is added

chunks.en: adds the days of Mashiach.
chunks.st: to include the days of the Messiah.

mishnayos.stIntro: It is a mitzva by Torah law to mention the exodus from Egypt at night, but some held that this mitzva was, like phylacteries or ritual fringes, fulfilled only during the day and not at night. For this reason it was decided:

mishnayos.summary: To do the mitzvah of Shema you must have in mind to do it. This mishnah also teaches when you may stop in the middle of Shema to greet someone.

chunks.en: If someone was reading the Torah
chunks.st: One who was reading the sections of the Torah which comprise Shema,

chunks.en: and the time came to say Shema,
chunks.st: and the time for the recitation of the morning or evening Shema arrived,

chunks.en: if he had in mind to do the mitzvah,
chunks.st: if he focused his heart,

chunks.en: he did the mitzvah. And if not,
chunks.st: he fulfilled his obligation
chunks.basisNote: Steinsaltz's text stops at 'he did the mitzvah'; 'and if not' follows Bartenura.

chunks.en: he did not do the mitzvah.
chunks.st: and need not repeat Shema in order to fulfill his obligation.
chunks.stMore: This is true even if he failed to recite the requisite blessings (Rabbeinu Ḥananel). Ab initio, one may not interrupt the recitation of Shema. The tanna’im, however, disagree over how strict one must be in this regard. They distinguish between interruptions between paragraphs and interruptions within each paragraph.
chunks.basisNote: Steinsaltz's text does not have these words; following Bartenura.

chunks.en: Between the sections, he may greet someone out of respect, and answer,
chunks.st: At the breaks between paragraphs, one may greet an individual due to the respect that he is obligated to show him, and one may respond to another’s greeting due to respect.

chunks.en: and in the middle, he may greet someone he fears, and answer.
chunks.st: And in the middle of each paragraph one may greet an individual due to the fear that the individual may harm him if he fails do so (Me’iri) and one may respond to another’s greeting due to fear.

words.note: Someone he is afraid of, like a king or a dangerous person.

chunks.en: These are the words of Rabbi Meir.
chunks.st: This is the statement of Rabbi Meir.

words.note: A great Rabbi of the Mishnah.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:
chunks.stMore: There is a distinction between greeting someone and responding to his greeting.

words.note: A great Rabbi of the Mishnah.

chunks.en: in the middle he may greet someone he fears,
chunks.st: In the middle of each paragraph, one may greet another due to fear

chunks.en: and answer someone he respects;
chunks.st: and respond due to respect.

chunks.en: between the sections he may greet someone he respects,
chunks.st: In the breaks between paragraphs, one may greet another due to respect

chunks.en: and answer "Shalom" to anyone.
chunks.st: and respond with a greeting to any person who greets him, whether or not he is obligated to show him respect.

mishnayos.stIntro: The first question discussed in the mishna is the question of intent.

mishnayos.summary: This mishnah lists the places "between the sections" of Shema and its brachos, and explains why the parts of Shema are in their order.

chunks.en: These are the places "between the sections":
chunks.st: these are the breaks between the paragraphs:

chunks.en: between the first bracha and the second,
chunks.st: Between the first blessing and the second,

chunks.en: between the second and Shema,
chunks.st: between the second and Shema,

chunks.en: and between Shema and "Vehayah im shamoa,"
chunks.st: between Shema and the second paragraph: If you indeed heed My commandments [VeHaya im Shamoa],

words.note: The second paragraph of Shema.

chunks.en: between "Vehayah im shamoa" and "Vayomer,"
chunks.st: between VeHaya im Shamoa and the third paragraph: And the Lord spoke [VaYomer]

words.note: The third paragraph of Shema, about tzitzis.

chunks.en: between "Vayomer" and "Emes Veyatziv."
chunks.st: and between VaYomer and True and Firm [emet veyatziv], the blessing that follows Shema.
chunks.stMore: The Rabbis held that each blessing and each paragraph of Shema constitutes its own entity, and treat interruptions between them as between the paragraphs.

words.note: The bracha right after Shema in the morning.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda, however, says:

words.note: A great Rabbi of the Mishnah.

chunks.he: בֵּין וַיֹּאמֶר לֶאֱמֶת וְיַצִּיב לֹא יַפְסִיק.
chunks.en: between "Vayomer" and "Emes Veyatziv" one may not stop.
chunks.st: Between VaYomer and emet veyatziv, which begins the blessing that follows Shema, one may not interrupt at all.
chunks.stMore: According to Rabbi Yehuda, these must be recited consecutively. Since the paragraphs of Shema are not adjacent to one another in the Torah, and they are not recited in the order in which they appear, the mishna explains their placement.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korchah said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korḥa said:

words.note: A great Rabbi of the Mishnah.

chunks.he: לָמָּה קָדְמָה שְׁמַע לִוְהָיָה אִם שָׁמֹעַ,
chunks.en: Why does Shema come before "Vehayah im shamoa"?
chunks.st: Why, in the mitzva of the recitation of Shema, did the portion of Shema precede that of VeHaya im Shamoa?

chunks.en: So that a person will accept
chunks.st: This is so that one will first accept upon himself

chunks.en: Hashem as his King first,
chunks.st: the yoke of the kingdom of Heaven, the awareness of God and God’s unity,

words.note: Accepting Hashem as our King.

chunks.he: וְאַחַר כָּךְ יְקַבֵּל עָלָיו עֹל מִצְוֹת.
chunks.en: and after that he accepts the mitzvos.
chunks.st: and only then accept upon himself the yoke of the mitzvot, which appears in the paragraph of VeHaya im Shamoa.

chunks.en: And "Vehayah im shamoa" comes before "Vayomer,"
chunks.st: Why did VeHaya im Shamoa precede VaYomer?

chunks.he: שֶׁוְהָיָה אִם שָׁמֹעַ נוֹהֵג בַּיּוֹם וּבַלַּיְלָה,
chunks.en: because "Vehayah im shamoa" applies day and night,
chunks.st: Because the paragraph of VeHaya im Shamoa is practiced both by day and by night,

chunks.en: but "Vayomer" only applies in the daytime.
chunks.st: while VaYomer, which discusses the mitzva of ritual fringes, is only practiced during the day.

words.note: Because it is about tzitzis, which we wear in the daytime.

mishnayos.stIntro: As for what constitutes a paragraph,

mishnayos.summary: This mishnah teaches what happens if you say Shema too quietly, unclearly, out of order, or with a mistake.

chunks.he: הַקּוֹרֵא אֶת שְׁמַע וְלֹא הִשְׁמִיעַ לְאָזְנוֹ,
chunks.en: If someone says Shema so quietly that his own ears cannot hear it,
chunks.st: One who recites Shema and did not recite in a manner audible to his own ear,
chunks.stMore: either because he read inaudibly or because he is deaf,

chunks.en: he did the mitzvah. Rabbi Yosi says,
chunks.st: fulfilled his obligation. Rabbi Yosei says:

words.note: A great Rabbi of the Mishnah.

chunks.en: he did not do the mitzvah.
chunks.st: He did not fulfill his obligation.

chunks.en: If he read without saying each letter carefully,
chunks.st: One who recited Shema and was not sufficiently precise in his enunciation of its letters,

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosi says he did the mitzvah,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei says: He fulfilled his obligation.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says he did not.
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says: He did not fulfill his obligation.

words.note: A great Rabbi of the Mishnah.

chunks.en: If someone reads it out of order,
chunks.st: One who recited Shema out of order, meaning he did not read the verses sequentially,

chunks.en: he did not do the mitzvah.
chunks.st: he did not fulfill his obligation.

chunks.en: If he read and made a mistake,
chunks.st: One who recited and erred,

chunks.en: he goes back to the place of the mistake.
chunks.st: should return to the place in Shema that he erred.

mishnayos.summary: Workers may say Shema while up in a tree or on a wall, but they must come down to daven Shemoneh Esrei.

chunks.en: Workers may say Shema at the top of a tree
chunks.st: Laborers engaged in their work may recite Shema while standing atop the tree

chunks.en: or at the top of a row of stones in a wall,
chunks.st: or atop the course of stones in a wall under construction,

words.note: A row of stones in a wall that is being built.

chunks.he: מַה שֶּׁאֵינָן רַשָּׁאִין לַעֲשׂוֹת כֵּן בַּתְּפִלָּה:
chunks.en: which they may not do for davening Shemoneh Esrei.
chunks.st: which they are not permitted to do for the Amida prayer, which requires intent of the heart.

words.note: Here "tefillah" means Shemoneh Esrei.

mishnayos.stIntro: The primary issue in this mishna is the requisite degree of concentration when reciting Shema.

mishnayos.summary: A chassan does not have to say Shema on his wedding night, because he is too busy thinking. But Rabban Gamliel said it anyway, because he did not want to stop accepting Hashem as King even for a moment.

chunks.en: A chassan does not have to say Shema at night
chunks.st: A groom is exempt from the recitation of Shema on

words.note: A chassan is a groom who just got married.

chunks.en: on the first night after his wedding, until after Shabbos,
chunks.st: the first night of his marriage, which was generally Wednesday night, until Saturday night,

chunks.en: if he has not yet done the act of marriage.
chunks.st: if he has not taken action and consummated the marriage,
chunks.stMore: as he is preoccupied by concerns related to consummation of the marriage. The mishna relates that

chunks.en: There was a story with Rabban Gamliel, who said Shema
chunks.st: there was an incident where Rabban Gamliel married a woman and recited Shema

words.note: A great Rabbi of the Mishnah, head of the Sanhedrin.

chunks.en: on the first night after he got married.
chunks.st: even the first night.

chunks.en: His students said to him,
chunks.st: His students said to him:

chunks.en: "Didn't you teach us,
chunks.st: Didn’t our teacher teach us

chunks.he: רַבֵּנוּ, שֶׁחָתָן פָּטוּר מִקְּרִיאַת שְׁמַע בַּלַּיְלָה הָרִאשׁוֹן.
chunks.en: our Rebbi, that a chassan does not have to say Shema on the first night?"
chunks.st: that a groom is exempt from the recitation of Shema?

chunks.en: He said to them,
chunks.st: He answered them:

chunks.en: "I will not listen to you and take off from myself
chunks.st: Nevertheless, I am not listening to you to refrain from reciting Shema, and in so doing preclude myself from the acceptance of

chunks.en: Hashem as my King, even for one moment."
chunks.st: the yoke of the Kingdom of Heaven, for even one moment.

words.note: Accepting Hashem as our King.

mishnayos.stIntro: The mishna continues:

mishnayos.summary: Rabban Gamliel washed himself on the first night after his wife died, even though a mourner may not wash. He explained that he was a very delicate person who would suffer without washing.

chunks.en: He washed on the first night after his wife died.
chunks.st: He bathed on the first night after his wife died.

chunks.en: His students said to him,
chunks.st: His students said to him:

chunks.en: "Didn't you teach us,
chunks.st: Have you not taught us,

chunks.en: our Rebbi, that a mourner may not wash?"
chunks.st: our teacher, that a mourner is prohibited to bathe?

words.note: An avel is someone whose close relative just died.

chunks.en: He said to them,
chunks.st: He answered them:

chunks.en: "I am not like all other people,
chunks.st: I am not like other people,

chunks.en: I am very delicate."
chunks.st: I am delicate [istenis].
chunks.stMore: For me, not bathing causes actual physical distress, and even a mourner need not suffer physical distress as part of his mourning.
chunks.basisNote: Steinsaltz: delicate. Bartenura: he caught cold easily and would suffer.

words.note: Someone so sensitive that not washing would make him sick.

mishnayos.stIntro: The mishna relates another episode portraying unusual conduct by Rabban Gamliel.

mishnayos.summary: When Rabban Gamliel's servant Tavi died, he accepted comforting like for a family member. He explained that Tavi was a very special, righteous servant.

chunks.en: And when Tavi, his servant, died,
chunks.st: And when his slave, Tavi, died,

chunks.en: he let people come comfort him.
chunks.st: Rabban Gamliel accepted condolences for his death as one would for a close family member.

words.note: Words of comfort said to a mourner.

chunks.en: His students said to him,
chunks.st: His students said to him:

chunks.en: "Didn't you teach us, our Rebbi,
chunks.st: Have you not taught us, our teacher,

chunks.en: that we do not accept comforting for servants?"
chunks.st: that one does not accept condolences for the death of slaves?

chunks.en: He said to them,
chunks.st: Rabban Gamliel said to his students:

chunks.he: אֵין טָבִי עַבְדִּי כִּשְׁאָר כָּל הָעֲבָדִים,
chunks.en: "My servant Tavi is not like all other servants;
chunks.st: My slave, Tavi, is not like all the rest of the slaves,

chunks.en: he was a good, honest man."
chunks.st: he was virtuous
chunks.stMore: and it is appropriate to accord him the same respect accorded to a family member.

mishnayos.stIntro: Another exceptional incident is related:

mishnayos.summary: A chassan may say Shema on his first night if he wants. Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says not everyone should act as if he is so holy that he can concentrate.

chunks.en: A chassan, if he wants to say
chunks.st: if, despite his exemption, a groom wishes to recite

words.note: A groom who just got married.

chunks.en: Shema on the first night,
chunks.st: Shema on the first night,

chunks.he: קוֹרֵא. רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר,
chunks.en: may say it. Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says,
chunks.st: he may do so. Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:

words.note: A great Rabbi of the Mishnah, head of the Sanhedrin.

chunks.en: Not everyone who wants to take
chunks.st: Not everyone who wishes to assume

chunks.en: the name of being very holy may take it.
chunks.explain: Acting extra holy when people don't see you that way is showing off.
chunks.st: the reputation of a God-fearing person may assume it,
chunks.stMore: and consequently, not everyone who wishes to recite Shema on his wedding night may do so.

words.note: A name for being a very holy, God-fearing person.

mishnayos.stIntro: With regard to the recitation of Shema on one’s wedding night, the Sages said that

mishnayos.summary: Someone whose close relative just died and is not yet buried is too busy to say Shema, daven, or put on tefillin. The people carrying the coffin also don't say Shema if they are needed.

chunks.en: Someone whose dead relative is lying in front of him, not yet buried,
chunks.st: One whose deceased relative is laid out unburied before him

chunks.en: does not have to say Shema,
chunks.st: is exempt from the recitation of Shema,

chunks.en: or daven Shemoneh Esrei, or put on tefillin.
chunks.st: from the Amida prayer, and from the mitzva to don phylacteries, until the deceased has been buried.

words.note: The main prayer we say standing, also called the Amidah.

chunks.en: The people who carry the coffin, the ones who take their place, and the ones who take their place after that,
chunks.st: With regard to the pallbearers and their replacements and the replacements of their replacements,

words.note: The bed or stretcher the person who died is carried on.

chunks.he: אֶת שֶׁלִּפְנֵי הַמִּטָּה וְאֶת שֶׁלְּאַחַר הַמִּטָּה,
chunks.en: both those walking in front of the coffin and those behind it,
chunks.st: those located before the bier who have not yet carried the deceased and those located after the bier.

chunks.en: the ones who are needed to carry it do not have to say Shema,
chunks.st: Those who are needed to carry the bier are exempt from reciting Shema;

chunks.he: וְאֶת שֶׁאֵין לַמִּטָּה צֹרֶךְ בָּהֶן חַיָּבִין.
chunks.en: but the ones who are not needed to carry it must say Shema.
chunks.st: while those who are not needed to carry the bier, are obligated to recite Shema.

chunks.en: Both groups do not have to daven Shemoneh Esrei.
chunks.st: However, both these and those are exempt from reciting the Amida prayer,
chunks.stMore: since they are preoccupied and are unable to focus and pray with the appropriate intent.

mishnayos.summary: After a funeral, people may start Shema only if they can finish before they reach the rows of people comforting the mourners. In those rows, only the people in the inside row are free from saying Shema.

chunks.en: If they buried the person who died and came back,
chunks.st: After they buried the deceased and returned,

chunks.en: if they can start and finish saying Shema
chunks.st: if they have sufficient time to begin to recite Shema and conclude
chunks.basisNote: Steinsaltz: finish all of Shema. Bartenura: finish just one section of it.

chunks.en: before they get to the rows of people,
chunks.st: before they arrive at the row,
chunks.stMore: formed by those who attended the burial, through which the bereaved family will pass in order to receive consolation,

words.note: After a burial, people stand in rows so the mourners can walk between them and be comforted.

chunks.en: they should start.
chunks.st: they should begin.

chunks.en: But if not, they should not start.
chunks.st: If they do not have sufficient time to conclude reciting the entire Shema, then they should not begin.

chunks.en: Of the people standing in the rows,
chunks.st: And those standing in the row,

chunks.en: the ones in the inside row do not have to say Shema,
chunks.st: those in the interior row, directly before whom the mourners will pass and who will console them, are exempt from reciting Shema,

words.note: The ones right next to the mourners, who comfort them.

chunks.en: but the ones in the outside row must say it.
chunks.st: while those in the exterior row, who stand there only to show their respect, are obligated to recite Shema.

mishnayos.summary: Women, slaves, and children don't have to say Shema or wear tefillin. But they do have to daven, have a mezuzah, and bentch after eating.

chunks.en: Women, slaves, and children do not have to
chunks.st: Women, slaves and minors are exempt

words.note: Servants who belonged to a Jewish master and kept some mitzvos.

chunks.en: say Shema or put on tefillin,
chunks.st: from the recitation of Shema and from phylacteries,

chunks.en: but they must daven and have a mezuzah,
chunks.st: but are obligated in prayer, mezuza

chunks.en: and bentch, the bracha after eating.
chunks.st: and Grace after Meals.

words.note: Bentching, the bracha said after eating bread.

mishnayos.summary: A man who is tamei from a certain kind of impurity may only think the Shema in his heart without saying the brachos. After food he says the bracha, but not before it. Rabbi Yehuda says he says the brachos before and after.

chunks.he: בַּעַל קֶרִי מְהַרְהֵר בְּלִבּוֹ וְאֵינוֹ מְבָרֵךְ,
chunks.en: A man who is tamei in a certain way thinks the Shema in his heart and does not say the brachos,
chunks.st: If the time for the recitation of Shema arrived and one is impure due to a seminal emission, he may contemplate Shema in his heart, but neither recites the blessings

words.note: A kind of impurity from the body; he must go to the mikvah before learning Torah.

chunks.en: not before it and not after it.
chunks.st: preceding Shema, nor the blessings following it.

chunks.en: And for food, he says the bracha after eating,
chunks.st: Over food which, after partaking, one is obligated by Torah law to recite a blessing, one recites a blessing afterward,

chunks.en: but he does not say the bracha before eating.
chunks.st: but one does not recite a blessing beforehand,
chunks.stMore: because the blessing recited prior to eating is a requirement by rabbinic law.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says,
chunks.st: And in all of these instances Rabbi Yehuda says:

words.note: Rabbi Yehuda was a great Rabbi of the Mishnah.

chunks.en: he says the brachos before them and after them.
chunks.explain: Both for Shema and for food.
chunks.st: He recites a blessing beforehand and thereafter in both the case of Shema and in the case of food.

mishnayos.stIntro: Ezra the Scribe decreed that one who is ritually impure because of a seminal emission may not engage in matters of Torah until he has immersed in a ritual bath and purified himself. This halakha was accepted over the course of many generations; however, many disputes arose with regard to the Torah matters to which it applies. Regarding this, the mishna says:

mishnayos.summary: If a man remembers in the middle of davening that he is tamei, he makes his davening shorter. If he went to the mikvah in the morning, he must cover himself before saying Shema. He may not say Shema in smelly water, and must stay four amos away from a dirty mess.

chunks.en: If a man was standing and davening,
chunks.st: One who was standing in prayer

chunks.en: and he remembered that he is tamei,
chunks.st: and he recalled that he experienced a seminal emission,
chunks.stMore: and according to this opinion he is prohibited from praying,

words.note: A kind of impurity from the body; he must go to the mikvah.

chunks.en: he should not stop,
chunks.st: should not interrupt his prayer,

chunks.en: but he should make each bracha shorter.
chunks.st: rather he should abridge each individual blessing.

chunks.en: If he went down into the mikvah to dip,
chunks.st: They stated a general principle: One who descended to immerse himself,

words.note: To go under the water of a mikvah to become tahor.

chunks.en: if he can come up, get dressed, and say Shema
chunks.st: if he is able to ascend, cover himself with a garment, and recite the morning Shema

chunks.en: before the sun comes up,
chunks.st: before sunrise,

chunks.en: he should come up, get dressed, and say it.
chunks.st: he should ascend, cover himself, and recite Shema,

chunks.en: And if not,
chunks.st: and if not,

chunks.en: he should cover himself with the water and say it there.
chunks.st: he should cover himself in the water and recite Shema there.

chunks.en: But he should not cover himself
chunks.st: He may not, however, cover himself

chunks.he: לֹא בַמַּיִם הָרָעִים וְלֹא בְמֵי הַמִּשְׁרָה,
chunks.en: not in smelly water and not in water where flax was soaking,
chunks.st: in either foul water, or water in which flax was soaked,

words.note: Water where flax plants were soaked, which smells bad.

chunks.en: until he pours fresh water into it.
chunks.st: until he pours other water into it.

chunks.en: And how far must he stay away from urine and from a dirty mess to say Shema?
chunks.st: And in general, how far must one distance himself from urine and feces in order to recite Shema?
chunks.basisNote: Both explain "them" as urine; Bartenura says some words are missing here.

words.note: Urine.

chunks.en: Four amos.
chunks.st: At least four cubits.

words.note: An amah is about the length of a grown-up's arm, about 2 feet.

mishnayos.stIntro: This mishna contains various statements with regard to individuals with different types of ritual impurity as well as the need to distance oneself from filth and impurity.

mishnayos.summary: Some people who are already tamei in a bigger way also became tamei in a smaller way. The Chachamim say they still need to go to the mikvah before davening and learning, but Rabbi Yehuda says they don't.

chunks.en: A zav who also became tamei from a seminal emission,
chunks.st: Consequently, even a zav, whose impurity lasts at least seven days, who experienced a seminal emission,
chunks.stMore: for which, were he not a zav, he would be impure for only one day;

words.note: A man who is tamei for at least seven days because of an illness.
Another kind of impurity from the body.

chunks.en: and a niddah who also became tamei in another way,
chunks.st: a menstruating woman who discharged semen,
chunks.stMore: despite the fact that she is already impure with a severe impurity unaffected by her immersion;

words.note: A woman who is tamei for at least seven days at certain times of the month.

chunks.en: and a married woman who became a niddah,
chunks.st: and a woman who engaged in conjugal relations with her husband and later saw menstrual blood,

words.en: and a woman with her husband

chunks.en: all need to go to the mikvah.
chunks.explain: Before learning Torah or davening.
chunks.st: all require immersion.

chunks.en: But Rabbi Yehuda says they don't have to.
chunks.st: And Rabbi Yehuda exempts them from immersion.

words.note: Rabbi Yehuda was a great Rabbi of the Mishnah.

mishnayos.stIntro: Continuing the earlier discussion of the halakhot of immersion for Torah study and prayer for one who experienced a seminal emission, the mishna discusses a case where individuals who were already impure with a severe form of ritual impurity are exposed to the impurity of a seminal emission as well. They are required to immerse themselves and purify themselves of the impurity of the seminal emission even though they remain impure due to the more severe impurity.

mishnayos.summary: This mishnah tells us until what time we may daven each tefillah: Shacharis, Mincha, Maariv, and Musaf.

chunks.en: The morning tefillah, Shacharis, may be said until midday.
chunks.st: the morning prayer may be recited until noon.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

words.note: Rabbi Yehuda was a great Rabbi of the Mishnah.

chunks.en: until four hours into the day.
chunks.st: It may be recited only until four hours after sunrise.

words.note: Hours counted from sunrise, about a third of the day.

chunks.en: The tefillah of Mincha may be said until evening.
chunks.st: According to the Rabbis, the afternoon prayer may be recited until the evening.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

words.note: Rabbi Yehuda was a great Rabbi of the Mishnah.

chunks.en: until plag haMincha, the middle of the late afternoon.
chunks.explain: About an hour and a quarter before night.
chunks.st: It may be recited only until the midpoint of the afternoon [pelag haminḥa],
chunks.stMore: i.e., the midpoint of the period that begins with the sacrifice of the daily afternoon offering and ends at nightfall, which is the end of the afternoon.
chunks.basisNote: The time amount is from Bartenura.

words.note: Plag haMincha, a little over an hour before nightfall.

chunks.en: The evening tefillah, Maariv, has no set time; it may be said all night.
chunks.st: The evening prayer may be recited throughout the night and is not fixed to a specific hour.
chunks.basisNote: Bartenura adds: the wording hints Maariv was once optional; today it is a must.

chunks.en: And Musaf may be said all day.
chunks.st: According to the Rabbis, the additional prayer may be recited all day.

words.note: The extra tefillah on Shabbos, Yom Tov, and Rosh Chodesh.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

words.note: Rabbi Yehuda was a great Rabbi of the Mishnah.

chunks.en: until seven hours into the day.
chunks.st: It may be recited only until seven hours after sunrise.

mishnayos.stIntro: This mishna determines the times beyond which the different prayers may not be recited. According to the Rabbis,

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Nechunya ben Hakanah said a short tefillah when he went into the beis midrash and when he left. Going in, he asked not to make any mistakes, and going out, he thanked Hashem for his share in learning.

chunks.he: רַבִּי נְחוּנְיָא בֶּן הַקָּנָה הָיָה מִתְפַּלֵּל
chunks.en: Rabbi Nechunya ben Hakanah used to daven
chunks.st: Rabbi Neḥunya ben Hakana would recite

words.note: Rabbi Nechunya ben Hakanah was a great Rabbi of the Mishnah.

chunks.he: בִּכְנִיסָתוֹ לְבֵית הַמִּדְרָשׁ וּבִיצִיאָתוֹ תְּפִלָּה קְצָרָה.
chunks.en: a short tefillah when he went into the beis midrash and when he left it.
chunks.st: a brief prayer upon his entrance into the study hall and upon his exit.

words.note: The beis midrash, where people learn Torah.

chunks.en: They asked him,
chunks.st: They said to him:

chunks.en: what is this tefillah for?
chunks.st: The study hall is not a dangerous place that would warrant a prayer when entering and exiting, so what room is there for this prayer?

chunks.en: He told them,
chunks.st: He said to them:

chunks.en: When I go in, I daven
chunks.st: Upon my entrance, I pray

chunks.en: that nothing should go wrong because of me,
chunks.explain: Like making a mistake in a halacha.
chunks.st: that no mishap will transpire caused by me in the study hall.
chunks.basisNote: The example is from Bartenura.

chunks.he: וּבִיצִיאָתִי אֲנִי נוֹתֵן הוֹדָיָה עַל חֶלְקִי:
chunks.en: and when I go out, I thank Hashem for my share.
chunks.explain: That he gets to sit and learn Torah.
chunks.st: And upon my exit, I give thanks for my portion.
chunks.basisNote: The explain is from Bartenura.

mishnayos.stIntro: In addition to the halakhot relating to the fixed prayers, the Gemara relates:

mishnayos.summary: Rabban Gamliel says we must say all of Shemoneh Esrei every day. Rabbi Yehoshua says a short version is enough, and Rabbi Akiva says it depends on whether the person knows it well.

chunks.en: Rabban Gamliel says,
chunks.st: Rabban Gamliel says:

words.note: Rabban Gamliel was the leader of the Jewish people in the time of the Mishnah.

chunks.he: בְּכָל יוֹם מִתְפַּלֵּל אָדָם שְׁמֹנֶה עֶשְׂרֵה.
chunks.en: every day a person davens Shemoneh Esrei.
chunks.st: Each and every day a person recites the prayer of eighteen blessings.

words.note: Shemoneh Esrei, the tefillah of eighteen brachos.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehoshua says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehoshua says:

words.note: Rabbi Yehoshua was a great Rabbi of the Mishnah.

chunks.en: a short version of Shemoneh Esrei.
chunks.st: A short prayer is sufficient, and one only recites an abridged version of the prayer of eighteen blessings.

chunks.en: Rabbi Akiva says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Akiva says an intermediate opinion:

words.note: Rabbi Akiva was a great Rabbi of the Mishnah.

chunks.en: if he knows his tefillah smoothly by heart,
chunks.st: If he is fluent in his prayer,

chunks.en: he should daven all of Shemoneh Esrei.
chunks.st: he recites the prayer of eighteen blessings,

chunks.en: And if not,
chunks.st: and if not,

chunks.en: a short version of Shemoneh Esrei.
chunks.st: he need only recite an abridged version of the prayer of eighteen blessings.

mishnayos.stIntro: The mishna cites a dispute with regard to the obligation to recite the Amida prayer, also known as Shemoneh Esreh, the prayer of eighteen blessings, or simply as tefilla, prayer.

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Eliezer teaches that davening must not be like a chore, but should be asking Hashem from the heart. Rabbi Yehoshua gives a short tefillah for someone traveling in a dangerous place.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer says:

words.note: Rabbi Eliezer was a great Rabbi of the Mishnah.

chunks.en: someone who makes his davening like a fixed chore,
chunks.st: One whose prayer is fixed,
chunks.basisNote: "Like a chore" is Bartenura's explanation; Steinsaltz just says "fixed."

chunks.en: his davening is not a real request for mercy.
chunks.st: his prayer is not supplication and is flawed.
chunks.stMore: The Gemara will clarify the halakhic implications of this flaw.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehoshua says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehoshua says:

words.note: Rabbi Yehoshua was a great Rabbi of the Mishnah.

chunks.en: someone who is walking in a dangerous place
chunks.st: One who cannot recite a complete prayer because he is walking in a place of danger,

chunks.en: says a short tefillah.
chunks.st: recites a brief prayer

chunks.en: He says: Hashem, save Your people,
chunks.st: and says: Redeem, Lord, Your people,

chunks.en: the ones left of the Jewish people.
chunks.st: the remnant of Israel,

chunks.he: בְּכָל פָּרָשַׁת הָעִבּוּר יִהְיוּ צָרְכֵיהֶם לְפָנֶיךָ.
chunks.en: At every time of change, may their needs be before You.
chunks.explain: Bartenura says it means: even when they sin.
chunks.st: at every transition [parashat ha’ibur], the meaning of which will be discussed in the Gemara. May their needs be before You.
chunks.basisNote: Steinsaltz leaves the meaning to the Gemara; Bartenura: when they stray into sin.

words.note: Steinsaltz: "every transition." Bartenura: when they stray into sin.

chunks.en: Blessed are You, Hashem, Who hears tefillah.
chunks.st: Blessed are You, Lord, Who listens to prayer.

mishnayos.summary: When we daven, we face toward the Beis HaMikdash. Someone riding a donkey should get off; if he can't, he turns his face, and if he can't do that, he thinks about the Kodesh HaKodashim.

chunks.en: If he was riding on a donkey,
chunks.st: One who was riding on a donkey

chunks.en: he should get off to daven.
chunks.st: should dismount and pray calmly.

chunks.en: And if he cannot get off,
chunks.st: If he is unable to dismount,

chunks.en: he should turn his face toward the Beis HaMikdash.
chunks.st: he should turn his face toward the direction of the Temple.
chunks.basisNote: Bartenura says toward Yerushalayim.

chunks.he: וְאִם אֵינוֹ יָכוֹל לְהַחֲזִיר אֶת פָּנָיו,
chunks.en: and if he cannot turn his face,
chunks.st: If he is unable to turn his face,

chunks.en: he should point his heart
chunks.st: it is sufficient that he focus his heart

chunks.en: toward the Kodesh HaKodashim.
chunks.st: opposite the Holy of Holies.

words.note: The Kodesh HaKodashim, the holiest room in the Beis HaMikdash.

mishnayos.stIntro: While praying, one must face toward the direction of the Holy Temple.

mishnayos.summary: Someone traveling on a boat, wagon, or raft who can't turn to face Yerushalayim should think about the Kodesh HaKodashim while he davens.

chunks.en: If he was traveling in a boat
chunks.st: Similarly, one who was traveling in a ship

chunks.en: or in a wagon or on a raft,
chunks.explain: And he cannot turn to face Yerushalayim.
chunks.st: or on a wagon or on a raft [asda] and is unable to turn and face in the direction of Jerusalem,

chunks.en: he should point his heart
chunks.st: should focus his heart

chunks.en: toward the Kodesh HaKodashim.
chunks.st: opposite the Holy of Holies.

words.note: The Kodesh HaKodashim, the holiest room in the Beis HaMikdash.

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Elazar ben Azaryah says Musaf is said only with a community minyan. The Chachamim say it is said with or without one.

chunks.en: Rabbi Elazar ben Azaryah says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya says:

words.note: Rabbi Elazar ben Azaryah was a great Rabbi of the Mishnah.

chunks.he: אֵין תְּפִלַּת הַמּוּסָפִין אֶלָּא בְּחֶבֶר עִיר.
chunks.en: Musaf is said only in a town with a minyan.
chunks.st: The additional prayer is only recited in a city where there is a quorum of ten [ḥever ir].
chunks.basisNote: Bartenura: only with a group, not alone.

words.note: The extra tefillah on Shabbos, Yom Tov, and Rosh Chodesh.
A town with a minyan of ten.

chunks.en: And the Sages say,
chunks.st: The Rabbis say:

chunks.en: with a town minyan or without one.
chunks.st: One may recite the additional prayer with a ḥever ir or without a ḥever ir.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says in his name,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says another opinion in his name, the name of Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya:

words.note: Rabbi Yehuda was a great Rabbi of the Mishnah.

chunks.en: any place where there is a town minyan,
chunks.st: Any place where there is a ḥever ir,

words.note: A town's group of ten men.

chunks.en: a person davening alone does not have to say Musaf.
chunks.explain: The chazzan's Musaf counts for him.
chunks.st: an individual is completely exempt from reciting the additional prayer.
chunks.basisNote: The explain is from Bartenura.

mishnayos.summary: How to get ready for davening: think seriously first, and once you start, don't stop for anything.

chunks.en: We only stand up to daven
chunks.st: One may only stand and begin to pray

chunks.en: with a serious, humble feeling.
chunks.st: from an approach of gravity and submission.

words.note: A heavy head means a serious, humble mood.

chunks.he: חֲסִידִים הָרִאשׁוֹנִים הָיוּ שׁוֹהִים שָׁעָה אַחַת
chunks.en: The pious people of long ago would wait one hour
chunks.st: There is a tradition that the early generations of pious men would wait one hour,
chunks.stMore: in order to reach the solemn frame of mind appropriate for prayer,

words.note: Very holy people who did more than they had to.

chunks.he: וּמִתְפַּלְּלִים, כְּדֵי שֶׁיְּכַוְּנוּ אֶת לִבָּם לַמָּקוֹם.
chunks.en: and then daven, so they could turn their hearts to Hashem.
chunks.st: and then pray, so that they would focus their hearts toward their Father in Heaven.
chunks.stMore: Standing in prayer is standing before God and, as such,

words.note: "HaMakom" is a name for Hashem, Who is everywhere.

chunks.en: Even if the king says hello to him,
chunks.st: even if the king greets him,

chunks.en: he should not answer him.
chunks.st: he should not respond to him;

chunks.en: And even if a snake is wrapped around his heel,
chunks.st: and even if a snake is wrapped on his heel,

chunks.en: he should not stop davening.
chunks.st: he should not interrupt his prayer.

mishnayos.summary: Where in Shemoneh Esrei we add words about rain and the Havdalah prayer on Motzei Shabbos.

chunks.en: We mention Hashem's power of rain in the bracha about bringing the dead back to life,
chunks.explain: This means saying Mashiv haruach umorid hageshem.
chunks.st: One mentions the might of the rains and recites: He makes the wind blow and the rain fall, in the second blessing of the Amida prayer, the blessing of the revival of the dead.

words.note: The second bracha of Shemoneh Esrei, "Mechayei Hameisim."

chunks.en: and we ask for rain in the bracha for the years,
chunks.explain: This means saying Vesein tal umatar.
chunks.st: And the request for rain: And grant dew and rain as a blessing, in the ninth blessing of the Amida prayer, the blessing of the years.

words.note: The bracha "Bareich Aleinu," asking for good crops.

chunks.en: and Havdalah goes in the bracha "Who grants knowledge" (Atah Chonen).
chunks.explain: On Motzei Shabbos we add Atah Chonantanu there.
chunks.st: And the prayer of distinction [havdala], between the holy and the profane recited in the evening prayer following Shabbat and festivals, in the fourth blessing of the Amida prayer: Who graciously grants knowledge.

words.note: Words that separate Shabbos or Yom Tov from the weekday.
The bracha "Atah Chonen," asking for wisdom.

chunks.en: Rabbi Akiva says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Akiva says:

words.note: A great Rabbi of the Mishnah.

chunks.en: it is said as a fourth bracha all by itself.
chunks.st: Havdala is recited as an independent fourth blessing.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer says, it goes in Modim, the thank-you bracha.
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer says that it is recited in the seventeenth blessing of the Amida prayer, the blessing of thanksgiving.

words.note: A great Rabbi of the Mishnah.
The bracha "Modim," where we thank Hashem.

mishnayos.stIntro: This mishna speaks of additions to the standard formula of the Amida prayer and the blessings in which they are incorporated.

mishnayos.summary: Some wrong things a chazzan might say, and what to do if the chazzan makes a mistake.

chunks.he: הָאוֹמֵר עַל קַן צִפּוֹר יַגִּיעוּ רַחֲמֶיךָ,
chunks.en: Someone who says, "Your mercy reaches even a bird's nest,"
chunks.st: One who recites in his supplication: Just as Your mercy is extended to a bird’s nest,
chunks.stMore: as You have commanded us to send away the mother before taking her chicks or eggs (Deuteronomy 22:6–7), so too extend Your mercy to us;

words.note: The mitzvah to send away a mother bird before taking the eggs.

chunks.en: or "May Your Name be mentioned for the good,"
chunks.st: and one who recites: May Your name be mentioned with the good

chunks.en: or "Modim, Modim," saying "we thank" twice,
chunks.st: or one who recites: We give thanks, we give thanks twice,

chunks.en: we make him stop.
chunks.explain: These words can give a wrong idea about Hashem.
chunks.st: they silence him.
chunks.stMore: This mishna and the next one deal with the communal prayer leader. (If one says: “May the good bless You,” this is a path of heresy.)

chunks.en: If the chazzan leading the davening makes a mistake,
chunks.st: One who is passing before the ark, as prayer leader, and erred,

words.note: The aron where the Sefer Torah is; the chazzan stands in front of it.

chunks.en: someone else should take his place right away,
chunks.st: another should immediately pass in his place,

chunks.en: and at that time he should not say "no thanks" to be polite.
chunks.explain: Usually, people politely say no when first asked to lead.
chunks.st: and at that moment, this replacement should not refuse in the interest of courtesy.
chunks.stMore: The Amida prayer was interrupted and he should replace him as quickly as possible.

chunks.en: Where does the new chazzan start?
chunks.st: From where does the replacement commence?

chunks.en: From the beginning of the bracha where the mistake was.
chunks.st: From the beginning of the blessing in which the former had erred.

mishnayos.stIntro: Concluding the laws of prayer in this tractate, the mishna raises several prayer-related matters. This mishna speaks of certain innovations in the prayer formula that warrant the silencing of a communal prayer leader who attempts to introduce them in his prayers, as their content tends toward heresy.

mishnayos.summary: The chazzan should be careful not to get mixed up, so he doesn't answer Amen to the Kohanim or do Birkas Kohanim himself.

chunks.en: The chazzan leading the davening
chunks.st: one who passes before the ark

words.note: The aron where the Sefer Torah is; the chazzan stands in front of it.

chunks.en: should not answer Amen after the Kohanim's bracha,
chunks.st: should not respond amen after the blessing of the priests,

words.note: Kohanim bless the people with Birkas Kohanim.

chunks.en: because he might get mixed up.
chunks.st: because of potential confusion.
chunks.stMore: Since the mishna is describing a situation in which he was praying without a prayer book, responding amen would interrupt the order of the prayer and potentially lead him to begin a different blessing.

chunks.he: וְאִם אֵין שָׁם כֹּהֵן אֶלָּא הוּא,
chunks.en: And even if the chazzan is the only Kohen there,
chunks.st: For this reason, even if there is no priest other than the communal prayer leader,

chunks.en: he should not raise his hands to bless the people.
chunks.st: he does not lift his hands to bless the people, lest he become confused.

chunks.en: But if he is sure
chunks.st: And, however, if he is certain

chunks.en: that he can raise his hands to bless
chunks.st: that he can lift his hands

chunks.en: and go back to his davening, he may do it.
chunks.st: and resume his prayer without becoming confused, he is permitted to recite the blessing.

mishnayos.stIntro: In order to prevent the prayer leader from erring in his prayer, it was said that

mishnayos.summary: A mistake in davening is a bad sign. Rabbi Chanina ben Dosa could tell if his prayers for sick people were accepted.

chunks.en: If someone davens and makes a mistake,
chunks.st: One who prays and realizes that he erred in his prayer,

chunks.en: it is a bad sign for him.
chunks.explain: It shows his tefillah was not accepted.
chunks.st: it is a bad omen for him;
chunks.stMore: it indicates to him that his prayer was not accepted.

chunks.en: And if he is the chazzan,
chunks.st: And if he who erred is the communal prayer leader,

words.note: The chazzan, who davens for everyone.

chunks.en: it is a bad sign for the people who sent him,
chunks.st: it is a bad omen for those who sent him,

chunks.en: because a person's messenger is like the person himself.
chunks.st: because a person’s agent has legal status equivalent to his own.

chunks.en: They said about
chunks.st: On a similar note, they said about

chunks.en: Rabbi Chanina ben Dosa,
chunks.st: Rabbi Ḥanina ben Dosa

words.note: A great Rabbi of the Mishnah, famous for his holy prayers.

chunks.en: that when he davened for sick people, he would say,
chunks.st: that he would pray on behalf of the sick and immediately after his prayer he would say:

chunks.en: "This one will live, and this one will die."
chunks.st: This one shall recover from his illness and live and this one shall die.

chunks.en: They asked him,
chunks.st: When they said to him:

chunks.en: "How do you know?"
chunks.st: From where do you know?

chunks.en: He told them,
chunks.st: He said to them:

chunks.en: "If my tefillah flows smoothly from my mouth,
chunks.st: If my prayer is fluent in my mouth as I recite it and there are no errors,

chunks.en: I know that it was accepted.
chunks.st: I know that my prayer is accepted.

chunks.en: And if not,
chunks.st: And if not,

chunks.en: I know that it was not accepted."
chunks.st: I know that my prayer is rejected.
chunks.basisNote: Bartenura's first explanation: the sick person is "torn away" and will not live.

mishnayos.stIntro: Concluding its discussion of the halakhot of prayer, the mishna discusses less practical aspects of prayer.

mishnayos.summary: Which bracha we make before eating fruit, wine, bread, and vegetables.

chunks.en: How do we make a bracha on fruits?
chunks.st: How does one recite a blessing over fruits?

chunks.en: On fruit from a tree, one says,
chunks.st: Over different fruits that grow on a tree one recites:

chunks.en: "Borei pri ha'etz" (Who creates fruit of the tree),
chunks.st: Who creates fruit of the tree,

chunks.en: except for wine,
chunks.st: with the exception of wine.
chunks.stMore: Although wine is produced from fruit of the tree, due to its significance, its blessing differs from other fruits of the tree.

chunks.he: שֶׁעַל הַיַּיִן אוֹמֵר בּוֹרֵא פְּרִי הַגָּפֶן.
chunks.en: because on wine one says "Borei pri hagafen" (Who creates fruit of the vine).
chunks.st: Over wine one recites: Who creates fruit of the vine.

chunks.en: And on fruits that grow from the ground, one says
chunks.st: Over fruits that grow from the earth, one recites:

chunks.en: "Borei pri ha'adamah" (Who creates fruit of the ground),
chunks.st: Who creates fruit of the ground,

chunks.en: except for bread,
chunks.st: with the exception of bread.
chunks.stMore: Bread, too, is significant and its blessing differs from other fruits of the ground,

chunks.en: because on bread one says
chunks.st: as over bread one recites:

chunks.en: "Hamotzi lechem min ha'aretz" (Who brings bread out of the earth).
chunks.st: Who brings forth bread from the earth.

chunks.he: וְעַל הַיְרָקוֹת אוֹמֵר בּוֹרֵא פְּרִי הָאֲדָמָה.
chunks.en: And on vegetables one says "Borei pri ha'adamah."
chunks.st: Over herbs and leafy vegetables one recites: Who creates fruit of the ground.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says
chunks.stMore: that there is room to distinguish between fruits that grow from the earth, herbs, and leafy vegetables. Although they are all fruit of the ground, since they have different qualities, the blessing on the latter is:

words.note: A great Rabbi of the Mishnah.

chunks.en: "Who creates many kinds of herbs."
chunks.st: Who creates various kinds of herbs.

mishnayos.stIntro: This mishna discusses the blessings recited over various foods.

mishnayos.summary: If you made the wrong bracha on food, sometimes it still counts, and "Shehakol" works for everything.

chunks.he: בֵּרַךְ עַל פֵּרוֹת הָאִילָן בּוֹרֵא פְּרִי הָאֲדָמָה,
chunks.en: If someone said "Borei pri ha'adamah" on fruit from a tree,
chunks.st: One who recited: Who creates fruit of the ground, over fruit of the tree,

chunks.en: he has done the mitzvah.
chunks.st: fulfilled his obligation.

words.note: He did the mitzvah and does not need to say it again.

chunks.he: וְעַל פֵּרוֹת הָאָרֶץ בּוֹרֵא פְּרִי הָעֵץ,
chunks.en: But if he said "Borei pri ha'etz" on fruits from the ground,
chunks.st: One who recited: Who creates fruit of the tree, over fruits of the earth,

chunks.en: he has not done the mitzvah.
chunks.st: did not fulfill his obligation.

chunks.he: עַל כֻּלָּם אִם אָמַר שֶׁהַכֹּל נִהְיָה, יָצָא:
chunks.en: On all foods, if he said "Shehakol," he has done the mitzvah.
chunks.st: And over all food items, one who recited: By whose word all things came to be, fulfilled his obligation.

words.note: The bracha "Shehakol," meaning everything came to be by Hashem's word.

mishnayos.stIntro: This mishna discusses how, after the fact, a more general blessing exempts one from the obligation to recite a more specific one.

mishnayos.summary: Foods that don't grow from the ground get the bracha "Shehakol."

chunks.he: עַל דָּבָר שֶׁאֵין גִּדּוּלוֹ מִן הָאָרֶץ
chunks.en: On something that does not grow from the ground
chunks.st: And over a food item whose growth is not from the ground,

chunks.en: one says "Shehakol."
chunks.st: one recites: By whose word all things came to be.

chunks.en: On vinegar, and on spoiled dates,
chunks.st: And over vinegar, wine that fermented and spoiled, and over novelot, dates that spoiled,
chunks.basisNote: Bartenura: novelos are fruits that fell from the tree before they were ripe.

words.note: Wine that went sour.
Dates that went bad.

chunks.en: and on locusts, one says "Shehakol."
chunks.st: and over locusts, one recites: By whose word all things came to be.

words.note: A kind of grasshopper; some kinds are kosher.

chunks.en: On milk and on cheese
chunks.st: So too, over milk, and over cheese,

chunks.en: and on eggs, one says "Shehakol."
chunks.st: and over eggs, one recites: By whose word all things came to be.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

words.note: A great Rabbi of the Mishnah.

chunks.en: anything that comes from a curse, like spoiled food,
chunks.st: Over any food item that is a type resulting from a curse,

chunks.en: we do not make a bracha on it.
chunks.st: one does not recite a blessing over it at all.
chunks.stMore: None of the items listed exist under normal conditions, and they come about as the result of a curse.

mishnayos.summary: If you have many foods in front of you, which one do you make the bracha on first?

chunks.en: If there were many kinds of food in front of him,
chunks.st: On a different note: If there were many types of food before him,
chunks.stMore: over which food should he recite a blessing first?

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

words.note: A great Rabbi of the Mishnah.

chunks.en: if one of them is from the seven special foods of Eretz Yisrael,
chunks.st: If there is one of the seven species for which Eretz Yisrael was praised among them,

words.note: The seven special foods of Eretz Yisrael, like grapes, figs, and dates.

chunks.en: he makes the bracha on that one first.
chunks.st: he recites the first blessing over it.

chunks.en: And the Sages say,
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say:

chunks.en: he makes the bracha on whichever one he wants.
chunks.st: He recites a blessing over whichever of them he wants.

mishnayos.summary: When one bracha covers other foods too, so you don't need a new bracha.

chunks.en: If he made a bracha on the wine before the meal,
chunks.st: One who recited a blessing over the wine that one drank before the meal,

chunks.en: it also covers the wine after the meal.
chunks.st: with that blessing he exempted the wine that he drinks after the meal.
chunks.basisNote: Bartenura says this is on Shabbos and Yom Tov, when wine is planned for after the meal.

words.note: He doesn't need another bracha for it.

chunks.en: If he made a bracha on the appetizers before the meal,
chunks.st: Similarly, one who recited a blessing over the appetizers that one ate before the meal,

words.note: Small foods eaten before or after a meal, like appetizers.

chunks.en: it also covers the appetizers after the meal.
chunks.st: with that blessing he exempted the appetizers that he eats after the meal.

chunks.en: If he made a bracha on the bread,
chunks.st: One who recited a blessing over the bread

chunks.en: it covers the appetizers,
chunks.st: exempted the appetizers, as they are considered secondary to the bread.

chunks.en: but a bracha on the appetizers
chunks.st: However, one who recited a blessing over the appetizers

chunks.en: does not cover the bread.
chunks.st: did not exempt the bread.

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say,
chunks.st: Beit Shammai say:

words.note: Beis Shammai are the students of Shammai, a great early Rabbi.

chunks.en: it does not even cover a cooked dish.
chunks.st: The blessing recited over the appetizers did not exempt even a cooked dish that he eats during the meal.

words.note: Food cooked in a pot.

mishnayos.stIntro: This mishna explains those cases and those circumstances in which blessings recited over particular foods exempt other foods at the meal from the requirement to recite a blessing over them.

mishnayos.summary: When people eat together, sometimes one person makes the bracha for everyone.

chunks.en: If people were sitting to eat, not as one group,
chunks.st: If several people were sitting to eat not in the framework of a joint meal,

chunks.en: each one makes his own bracha.
chunks.st: each recites a blessing for himself.

chunks.en: If they reclined together for a meal, one makes the bracha for all of them.
chunks.st: If they were reclined on divans to eat, which renders it a joint meal, one recites a blessing on behalf of them all.

words.note: Long ago, people ate a real meal together leaning on couches.

chunks.en: If wine was brought to them during the meal,
chunks.st: Additionally: If wine came before them during the meal,

chunks.en: each one makes his own bracha on it.
chunks.st: each and every diner recites a blessing over the wine for himself.

chunks.en: If it came after the meal,
chunks.st: If the wine came after the meal,

chunks.en: one makes the bracha for all of them.
chunks.st: one recites a blessing on behalf of them all.

chunks.en: And that same person says the bracha on the sweet-smelling incense,
chunks.st: And he, who recited the blessing over the wine, also says the blessing over the incense [mugmar],
chunks.basisNote: Steinsaltz: the one who blessed the wine. Bartenura: the one who led bentching.

words.note: Sweet-smelling spices burned on coals after a meal.

chunks.en: even though they only bring
chunks.st: although they only bring

chunks.en: the incense after the meal.
chunks.st: the incense to the diners after the meal.

mishnayos.stIntro: An additional halakha is cited:

mishnayos.summary: When one food is the main food and another is just a side, we make the bracha on the main food.

chunks.he: הֵבִיאוּ לְפָנָיו מָלִיחַ בַּתְּחִלָּה וּפַת עִמּוֹ,
chunks.en: If they brought him salty food first, with bread alongside it,
chunks.st: If they brought salted food before him to eat first and bread with it,

words.note: Salty food eaten after sweet fruit; bread helps him eat it.

chunks.he: מְבָרֵךְ עַל הַמָּלִיחַ וּפוֹטֵר אֶת הַפַּת,
chunks.en: he makes the bracha on the salty food, and that covers the bread,
chunks.st: he recites a blessing over the salted food and thereby exempts the bread,

chunks.en: because the bread is just a side to it.
chunks.explain: He only eats the bread to help him eat the salty food.
chunks.st: because the salted food is primary while the bread is secondary to it.

chunks.en: This is the rule:
chunks.st: This is the principle:

chunks.en: whenever there is a main food with a side food,
chunks.st: Any food that is primary and a secondary food is with it,

chunks.he: מְבָרֵךְ עַל הָעִקָּר וּפוֹטֵר אֶת הַטְּפֵלָה:
chunks.en: you make the bracha on the main food, and that covers the side food.
chunks.st: one recites a blessing over the primary and, in so doing, exempts the secondary from its own blessing.

mishnayos.summary: Which bracha to say after eating special fruits, vegetables, or drinking water.

chunks.en: If someone ate figs, grapes, and pomegranates,
chunks.st: One who ate from the fruit for which Eretz Yisrael was praised, grapes and figs and pomegranates,

chunks.en: he says after them the three brachos of bentching, like after bread,
chunks.st: recites the three blessings of Grace after Meals, as he would after eating bread;

words.note: The three main brachos of bentching after a bread meal.

chunks.en: so says Rabban Gamliel.
chunks.st: this is the statement of Rabban Gamliel.

words.note: "Rabban" is a title for the head of the Sages.
A great Rabbi of the Mishnah, the leader of the Sages.

chunks.en: And the Sages say,
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say:

chunks.en: only one bracha that is a short form of the three.
chunks.st: One need only recite one blessing abridged from the three blessings of Grace after Meals.

words.note: This is the short after-bracha, like Al Ha'etz.

chunks.en: Rabbi Akiva says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Akiva says:
chunks.stMore: The three blessings of Grace after Meals are not restricted to bread; rather,

words.note: A great Rabbi of the Mishnah.

chunks.en: even if he ate cooked vegetables and that is his main food,
chunks.st: even if one ate boiled vegetables, but it is his primary sustenance,

chunks.en: he says after it the three brachos of bentching.
chunks.st: he recites the three blessings of Grace after Meals.

chunks.en: Someone who drinks water because he is thirsty
chunks.st: Additionally: One who drinks water to quench his thirst

chunks.en: says "Shehakol nihyeh bidvaro" (everything came to be by His word).
chunks.st: recites: By whose word all things came to be.

chunks.en: Rabbi Tarfon says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Tarfon says:

words.note: A great Rabbi of the Mishnah.

chunks.en: "Borei nefashos rabos" (Who creates many living things and their needs).
chunks.st: He recites: Who creates the many forms of life and their needs.

mishnayos.summary: When three people eat a meal together, they must make a zimmun before bentching. The mishnah lists who counts toward the three and who does not.

chunks.en: Three people who ate together
chunks.st: Three people who ate as one

chunks.en: must make a zimmun.
chunks.st: are required to form a zimmun and recite Grace after Meals.

words.note: Inviting the others to bentch together, saying "Let us bless."
